runs.scope: Weekly planning, time entries, calendar rollovers and CSV exports.
runs.summary: Editing a time entry can erase its duration. Three further findings affect saved preferences, exports and month boundaries.
notRead: The hosted billing adapter requires a service account.
Mobile clients were outside the web workspace scope.
runs.board: Three findings link to existing work. A28 records the calendar defect discovered during this audit.

coverage.evidence: Followed create, edit and restore paths through the store and local persistence.
Checked both settings entry points and the first render after reload.
Compared rows at the pagination boundary with the exported file.
The local fixture has no service account.
This audit covers the web workspace.

findings.title: Editing a note erases the logged duration
findings.failure: Change the note on a 42-minute entry and save. The weekly total drops by 42 minutes.
evidence: The note editor omits duration when it submits a partial update.
The update path stores entry.total = 0 when duration is absent. Reloading confirms the persisted loss.
findings.fix: Retain the existing duration when the patch omits it. Cover a note-only edit in the store test.

findings.title: The planner forgets the chosen start of week
findings.failure: Choose Monday, reload the workspace and reopen the planner. The grid starts on Sunday.
evidence: The settings panel saves the new value to preferences.weekStart.
The initial planner state reads defaults, so weekStart resets to Sunday after a reload.
findings.fix: Initialise the planner from the saved preference before building the grid.

findings.title: CSV export skips a row between pages
findings.failure: Export 19 rows with a page size of 10. The first row of the second page is missing.
evidence: The cursor already points to the next unconsumed row. The export loop increments it again.
In the pagination fixture, 19 rows become 18 in the downloaded CSV.
findings.fix: Resume at the returned cursor and assert all row IDs across two pages.

findings.title: March opens with two identical day labels
findings.failure: Open March after a non-leap February. Both leading cells show the first day of March.
evidence: The grid builder mutates the first date while padding the previous month.
In the month-boundary fixture, 01 Mar appears twice.
findings.fix: Clone the padding date before advancing it and assert both boundary labels.

strengths.title: Undo restores the original entry
strengths.evidence: src/time/undo.test.ts:48 compares the full restored record with the saved snapshot.
strengths.benefit: A mistaken deletion preserves the entry's project, duration and original timestamp after undo.

ticketReviews.evidence: The B12 regression test passed at the closing revision 9b2d760. At c8a263f the same note-only update replaced 42 minutes with zero.

ticketReviews.expectation: The preferred start of week survives a reload.
ticketReviews.evidence: The value is saved, but the planner reads the default on first render.

ticketReviews.expectation: Export every row on both sides of the page boundary.
ticketReviews.evidence: The same row is missing in the existing ticket fixture.
All fields in the restored record matched the pre-delete snapshot.

proposals.title: Share the date-grid builder across calendar views
proposals.evidence: src/calendar/month.ts:37 and src/planner/grid.ts:18 calculate leading cells independently.
options: Keep both builders and add boundary tests to each.
Extract the date calculation into a shared function with a single fixture set.
